title: Google's new SynthID website can identify AI-generated media
key_facts: Google launched a site on Tuesday (6 Oct 2026) that lets anyone check whether an image, video or audio clip is AI-generated.
The tool was previously available to selected journalists, media professionals and researchers, tested at Google I/O last year; access is now open to everyone.
The site supports common image, video and audio formats, including JPG, PNG, MP4, MOV, WAV and MP3.
Google uses SynthID, introduced in 2023, to watermark media made by its Nano Banana, Veo and Lyria models and tools such as Gemini, Flow, ProducerAI and Vids.
OpenAI, Nvidia and Kakao also support SynthID; OpenAI maintains its own checking site; Apple is said to be adding support soon.
SynthID verification is built into the Gemini app and Google Chrome; Google says people make 1 million verification requests a day.
Microsoft and Meta have their own watermarking and verification standards, which TechCrunch says are not infallible and often fail to identify content made by their makers' models.
quote_evidence: Google on Tuesday launched a new site that lets anyone verify whether a piece of media, be it an image, a video, or an audio clip, is generated using AI.
The company said people currently make 1 million requests to verify content every day.
why_it_matters_hint: Anyone can now check AI-made images, videos and audio, which helps people and newsrooms spot fakes.
